title: Lumen Current: Signal Garden
tagline: Ride a living current of light and rekindle a drowning signal garden before the storm pressure snuffs it out.
pitch: You are a ribbon of bioluminescent light drifting through a dark, glass-floored conservatory. Three dormant signal nodes pulse faintly in the gloom while storm pressure rises and luminous pulse-waves sweep the garden. Weave between the pulses, reach each node and channel your light into it — three blooms and the garden wakes; let stability drain to zero and the current gutters out.
coreLoop: Steer the light current with Arrow/WASD across the single-screen garden, dodging expanding pressure pulses that drain stability on contact, and press Space while overlapping a dormant node to channel and activate it. Each activation lights up botanical circuitry, awards score, escalates hazard speed — and raises the stakes for the next node.

mechanics.name: Light Current Movement
mechanics.description: Smooth top-down movement (Arrow keys or WASD) with momentum and a trailing glow ribbon. The player is a bright outlined teardrop of light, always fully readable against the dark floor.

mechanics.name: Node Channeling
mechanics.description: Three signal nodes sit at fixed, generous-radius positions (roughly 70px activation radius) spread across the playfield. Standing inside a node's ring and pressing Space or Enter channels it for a fraction of a second, activating it: a bloom shockwave, vine-circuitry lights up toward the next node, +100 score, and objective progress advances.

mechanics.name: Storm Pulses
mechanics.description: Expanding luminous rings and drifting spore-orbs sweep the garden. Contact drains stability (the visible pressure resource). Their speed and spawn rate scale with a hazard multiplier that climbs with each node activated and steadily over time.

mechanics.name: Stability Pressure
mechanics.description: A visible stability bar (0-100) drains slowly on its own and sharply on pulse contact. At zero the run fails. This makes every detour a push-your-luck decision.

mechanics.name: Deterministic-Friendly Layout
mechanics.description: Nodes are placed along broad lanes so that generic directional sweeps and ordinary Space presses naturally cross them; activation radius is large and no precision aiming is ever required.

controls.keyboard: Arrow keys or WASD to move; Space or Enter to channel a node when overlapping it; Enter after a terminal state to start a fresh run.
controls.mouse: Pointer position shows a faint attraction shimmer (cosmetic); click near a node while overlapping also channels it.
controls.touch: Optional: virtual joystick left, tap right half to channel.

artDirection.mood: bioluminescent conservatory — dark glass, living light, elegant not militaristic
artDirection.backgroundFx: Two parallax layers of drifting botanical circuit-veins and slow-rising plankton motes over a subtly cycling deep-teal gradient; faint water-caustic shimmer across the glass floor.

audioDirection.musicMood: warm ambient pads with a soft pulse that quickens as pressure escalates

difficulty.start: Slow pulses, sparse spores, stability drains gently; first node is near the spawn lane.
difficulty.progression: Each node activation multiplies hazard speed (1.0 -> 1.35 -> 1.7) and pulse frequency; passive stability drain also steps up per node.
difficulty.peak: Third node: fast crossing pulses, dense spores, thin stability margin — a tense final dash.

winLose.win: Activate all three signal nodes -> success state with a blooming garden finale and score tally.
winLose.lose: Stability (visible pressure bar) reaches 0 -> failure state with the current guttering out.

juice.screenShake: Small 5px shake on pulse contact; 8px, 0.3s bloom-shake on node activation.
juice.particles: Burst of light motes on node bloom; drain sparks on pulse hit; gentle trailing sparks behind the current at most.
juice.hitStop: 60ms hit-stop on node activation for consequence; 40ms on pulse contact.
juice.flash: White-teal flash alpha 0.4 on node bloom; red-amber flash alpha 0.3 when stability crosses 25%.

scopeNotes: Cut: weapons/projectiles of any kind, enemies with health/combat, shops/inventory/upgrades/meta-progression, scrolling camera, multi-level structure, touch-specific calibration beyond optional stub, save files, narrative cutscenes. One screen, one run, three nodes.
signatureMoment: Node bloom: time hiccups, a shockwave of vine-circuitry races across the glass floor toward the next dormant node, lighting the garden segment by segment while the chime swells — the garden visibly comes alive with each activation.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: During an active run the player entity's position changes on the top-down 960x540 playfield in response to Arrow/WASD input, and Space/Enter performs the primary channel action.
Each of the three node activations increments the objective progress value (nodesActivated 0->3) and increases the run score by 100 per node.
After the third node is activated the game enters the success terminal state with visible victory UI.
When the visible stability resource reaches 0 the game enters the failure terminal state with visible failure UI.
Pressing Enter while in a terminal success or failure state starts a new run with nodesActivated reset to 0 and score reset.
The HUD renders at least three distinct non-overlapping regions showing node progress, the stability pressure bar, and score, positioned at screen edges away from the central play area.
The hazard speed multiplier is a real numeric gameplay value that increases during the run (e.g. 1.0 -> 1.35 -> 1.7 per node) and demonstrably speeds up pulse/spore motion.
No weapon-fire, shooting or combat event is ever emitted during any run.
No shop, inventory or equipment event or screen ever appears during any run.
Node activation never occurs without a player action: no node auto-activates while the player is idle or absent from its radius.

scoreEvents: +100 score per node activation (nodesActivated 1,2,3); optional +1 per second survived; no other score sources.

actionPolicy.designBoundary: Required deterministic gameplay must be reachable under generic bounded directional sweeps and ordinary action/pointer input; do not depend on hidden routes, target coordinates, precision-only aim, or verifier-specific backdoors.

scenarios.purpose: prove real successful completion under deterministic active input
prove real timeout/failure independently from success
